entities.summary: Shahi Tegin, Tegin Shah or Sri Shahi was a king of the Turk Shahis, a dynasty of Western Turk or mixed Western Turk-Hephthalite origin who ruled from Kabul and Kapisa to Gandhara in the 7th to 9th centuries. Born around 650 CE, Shahi Tegin's reign spanned from approximately 670 to 710 CE. He was a key figure in the region's politics and economy during the Islamic conquests. Shahi Tegin's empire played a crucial role in the Silk Road trade, controlling key routes between China and the Mediterranean. The king's military campaigns against the Umayyad Caliphate and the Byzantine Empire had significant consequences for the region's strategic balance. Shahi Tegin's legacy is also reflected in the cultural heritage of the Turk Shahis, with many of their architectural and artistic achievements still visible today. Despite the passage of time, Shahi Tegin's name remains an important part of the region's historical narrative, symbolizing the enduring power of local dynasties in the face of imperial expansion.
